house: Clann Fhearchair of Baile Mòr dhomhain
note: One of the seven houses of custody regrouped after the Sundering ({{date:III-0034}}). Its seat at {{place:burg:273}} gave Rodos the first king chosen by the houses ({{date:III-0058}}), and the double court near the mountain lasted as long as the house held the crown. After Sìleas nic Fhearchair the crown went to her son Uisdean mac Dhùghaill and his line.

members.name: Lachlann mac Fhearchair
members.note: Father of the first king of the house; the house roll gives his name and no more.

members.name: Fearchar mac Lachlainn
members.note: Chosen by the heads of the seven houses and crowned at Cathair dhearg {{date:III-0058}}; kept part of each year's court at Baile Mòr dhomhain.

members.name: Iain mac Lachlainn
members.note: The king's younger brother; kept the house's hall at Baile Mòr dhomhain in the seasons the court was away.

members.name: Fearchar Donn
members.note: Crowned after his father without dispute, {{date:III-0061}}.

members.name: Mòr nic Fhearchair
members.note: Sister of Fearchar Donn; given in marriage to a man of Clann Ìomhair at Dùn dhearg.

members.name: Gormshuil nic Iain
members.note: Named in the house roll among those who swore to Fearchar Donn.

members.name: Seumas mac Iain
members.note: A reeve of the house's grazing below the pass; nothing else is recorded.

members.name: Lachlann Òg mac Fhearchair
members.note: Elder brother of Sìleas; died young, before his father.

members.name: Sìleas nic Fhearchair
members.note: Queen after her father; fixed the firlot of Cathair dhearg, {{date:III-0069}}; reigned more than half a century.

members.name: Eilidh nic Sheumais
members.note: Kept the house roll at Baile Mòr dhomhain in Queen Sìleas's reign; the roll is lost and is known only from a later copy.

note: A custodian family of {{place:burg:88}} that gave the Council of Custodians its second high custodian under the humans ({{date:IV-0061}}), lost its seat on the council in the next generation, and sent the first Ròdaich child to an Tìr Thall ({{date:IV-0120}}).

members.name: Coinneach Glas
members.note: High custodian after Tormod mac Ailein; had never met a human before the Crossing and dealt with little else after it.

members.name: Eachann Mòr
members.note: A custodian of Ceann àrsaidh who lost his place on the council; sent his son west with the Mission's letter.

members.name: Iseabail nic Choinnich
members.note: Kept her father's copies of the council roll after his death.

members.name: Calum mac Eachainn
members.note: Sailed west on a Company ship, {{date:IV-0120}}, and is never recorded returning.

members.name: Ruairidh mac Eachainn
members.note: Held no seat on the council; the family's place there was not restored in the age.

members.name: Seònaid nic Eachainn
members.note: Kept the family's house at Ceann àrsaidh after her brother sailed.

members.name: Coinneach mac Ruairidh
members.note: A custodian of the town's shrine of Macha; his name is on the petitions of the Levy years.

members.name: Anna nic Ruairidh
members.note: Married inland; the family roll records that she went, but not where.

members.name: Tormod mac Choinnich
members.note: The last of the line the family roll records.

note: The line of the Company's overseers at {{place:burg:354}}. The Ròdaich gave the first of them the byname Maor, steward ({{date:IV-0092}}), and the staff and the byname went from father to son until Mòrag nic Iain Maor broke the staff at the Company's door ({{date:IV-0319}}).

members.name: Dòmhnall
members.note: A hewer of Muileann chrom; known only from his son's name.

members.name: Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, Raghnall Maor
members.note: A crew-leader since the first contract; the first overseer, given the Company's staff and a slate-roofed house, {{date:IV-0092}}.

members.name: Seonag nic Raghnaill
members.note: Kept her father's house after his death; not named in the Company's letters.

members.name: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor
members.note: Given his father's staff, {{date:IV-0137}}; signed the order that the camps keep no grain beyond a week's ration.

members.name: Iain Maor
members.note: Schooled at the Mission; kept his reports in the humans' tongue and his household in Ròdais; wrote against the night shift, {{date:IV-0243}}.

members.name: Ailean mac Dhòmhnaill
members.note: Worked the galleries under his brother's staff.

members.name: Ruairidh mac Iain
members.note: A hewer; the staff passed over him to his sister.

members.name: Mòrag nic Iain Maor
members.note: The first woman to hold the staff, {{date:IV-0258}}; fourth and last of her line to hold it.

members.name: Catrìona nic Iain
members.note: Sister of Mòrag Maor; kept the slate-roofed house after the staff was broken.

house: The keepers of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
note: The family that has kept the carters' house at the halfway stage of the coal road ({{place:marker:10}}) since Seònaid Bhàn reopened it ({{date:IV-0088}}). Her great-grandson Aonghas kept it through the years of the fortified houses ({{date:IV-0300}}).

members.name: Seònaid Bhàn
members.note: Reopened the house; the only keeper on the road who took both marks and barter.

members.name: Murchadh mac Phàdraig
members.note: Kept the house after his mother.

members.name: Peigi nic Phàdraig
members.note: Kept the byres and the carters' book.

members.name: Seònaid nic Mhurchaidh
members.note: Kept the house after her father, through the Levy and the Long Drought.

members.name: Ruairidh mac Mhurchaidh
members.note: A carter on the coal road.

members.name: Aonghas mac Dhùghaill
members.note: Great-grandson of Seònaid Bhàn; kept the house in the years the constables searched it most and found least.

members.name: Eilidh nic Dhùghaill
members.note: Served in the house under her brother.

members.name: Seumas mac Aonghais
members.note: Kept the house after his father under the restored kingdom.

house: Clann Choinnich of the silver guild
note: The family at the head of the refiners' guild that held the silver seam of {{place:burg:419}} against the Company ({{date:IV-0102}}) and kept it under the Silver Compact until the rising. Its name is the name of the house of custody that brought the silver petitions of the Sundering age, but no roll traces the descent.

members.name: Coinneach mac Dhonnchaidh
members.note: A refiner of the seam; the guild ledger names him among its members at the Crossing.

members.name: Ùna nic Choinnich
members.note: Led the guild; met the Company's surveyors at the adit with the whole guild and its ledgers; refused Martha Gale's partnership when very old, {{date:IV-0143}}.

members.name: Donnchadh mac Choinnich
members.note: Kept the guild's weights and ledgers under his sister.

members.name: Coinneach mac Alasdair
members.note: A refiner; carried the guild's bars to Seann Bhral.

members.name: Beathag nic Alasdair
members.note: Sat on the guild's council after her mother.

members.name: Iain mac Dhonnchaidh
members.note: Worked the new faces of the seam.

members.name: Ùna nic Choinnich Òg
members.note: Named for her grandmother; sat on the guild's council in the years it sold bar silver for marks.

members.name: Dòmhnall mac Iain
members.note: A refiner of the new town.

members.name: Ruairidh Ciar
members.note: Among the guild members who opened the armoury in {{year:IV-0337}}.

note: A human family descended, by its own account, from Thomas Pike, who kept the first tally-book of the trading post at {{place:burg:27}} ({{date:IV-0012}}) and held the Company alone after Harrow was lost. Its later members stayed on Rodos after the Severance and are counted among the Tuathaich of the north.

members.name: Thomas Pike
members.note: Trader at Ros dhomhain; partner of Harrow in the Company, and its sole holder from {{year:IV-0062}}.

members.name: John Pike
members.note: Clerk of the Company's post at Ros dhomhain.

members.name: Sarah Pike
members.note: Went home to an Tìr Thall and is not recorded returning.

members.name: Daniel Pike
members.note: A storekeeper on the northern concession.

members.name: Ann Pike
members.note: Married a farmer of the concession.

members.name: Matthew Pike
members.note: A miller of the northern concession.

members.name: William Pike
members.note: Stayed in the north at the Severance.

members.name: Agnes Pike
members.note: A Tuathaich teacher; opened the school at Doire ghlas with Moot money and without the council's leave, {{date:V-0066}}.

members.name: Joseph Pike
members.note: A fisherman of Caol mhòr.

note: The family of the first marriage in two tongues that any roll records, made at {{place:burg:105}} ({{date:IV-0028}}). The Moot's own genealogy traces its first speaker, Walter Hale, to that marriage. His great-grandson Peter Hale holds the Moot's chair in the present year ({{date:VI-0153}}).

members.name: Samuel Hale
members.spouse: Eilidh nic Ruairidh, net-maker of Baile dhìreach
members.note: A human cooper; his marriage was entered in both the council's books.

members.name: John Hale
members.note: A cooper of Baile dhìreach, like his father.

members.name: Mary Hale
members.note: A net-maker, like her mother.

members.name: Thomas Hale
members.note: Claimed a customary cutting through his Ròdaich grandmother and lost it by Dunstan's rule, {{date:IV-0231}}.

members.name: Richard Hale
members.note: A harbour hand in the north-west.

members.name: Walter Hale
members.note: A former harbour clerk; first speaker of the Moot at Caol mhòr, {{date:V-0008}}.

members.name: David Hale
members.note: Kept the Moot's minute-books in his father's time.

members.name: Alice Hale
members.note: Taught in one of the Moot's schools.

members.name: Frank Hale
members.note: A fisherman of Caol mhòr; father of Peter Hale.

house: The house of Mac Ùisdein of Cathair mhòr
note: A Ròdaich house of {{place:burg:23}} that held an overseer's post under the humans and the Sloc Mòr concession under the Crown ({{date:V-0051}}). It sold the concession back piece by piece, and it was the only house of the vein to move its money out before the vein failed it ({{date:VI-0042}}).

members.name: Ùisdean mac Ruairidh
members.note: Held the house's overseer's post under the Company; the post is the house's first entry in any roll.

members.name: Uisdean mac Ùisdein
members.note: Given the Sloc Mòr on the humans' terms with the names changed; raised the market cross and the stone house at Cathair mhòr.

members.name: Seonag nic Ùisdein
members.note: Kept the house's quarry accounts at Achadh dhomhain.

members.name: Ruairidh mac Uisdein
members.note: Held the house's share in his father's last years.

members.name: Dòmhnall mac Uisdein
members.note: Kept the quarry at Achadh dhomhain under the house's mark.

members.name: Catrìona nic Uisdein
members.note: Married at Cathair mhòr; took no part in the concession.

members.name: Alasdair mac Ùisdein
members.note: Grandson of the first holder; borrowed against the house's share for the search for a second vein, {{date:V-0174}}, and sold half the share to meet the debt.

members.name: Mòrag nic Ruairidh
members.note: Sister of Alasdair; kept the house's papers after the stone house was let to the Mine Board.
